context.firstUser: A teacher, streamer, coach, or group host preparing and running a random draw in front of other people.
context.primaryJob: Build a trustworthy numbered pool, choose the draw mode, run the pick, and confidently manage the pool afterward.
context.desiredResponse: The setup should feel as energetic and intentional as the winner reveal while remaining obvious, legible, and safe to operate live.
referenceProducts: Wheel of Names — keeps entries adjacent to the dominant randomizer and supports remove-after-pick behavior
Picker Wheel — separates input management, wheel state, and result actions while preserving direct manipulation
Kahoot! — combines high-energy classroom color with one dominant action and explicit participation state
artDirectionComparison: Restrained utility-clean: preserved sparse controls but rejected because it repeated the pale, generic system-button look the user wanted replaced.
Dark game-stage: amplified spectacle but rejected because it reduced sustained readability during roster entry and pool management.
Celebration-native light stage: selected because inked borders, hard depth, warm selection, and soft gradients carry winner-screen energy into the full workflow without hiding the work objects.

blurTest.evidence: At gallery scale, the contestant editor, draw setup, giant spin target, active pool, and upgrade decision remain distinct masses with one clear next action in each state.

silhouetteTest.evidence: The numbered roster feeding a two-mode randomizer and persistent pool actions creates a NameSnap-specific live-picker silhouette rather than a generic card dashboard.

fiveSecondTest.evidence: The header reports readiness or eligibility, the contestant editor explains one-name-per-line entry, and selected draw mode plus primary action are unmistakable on phone and tablet.

realityTest.evidence: Fresh simulator renders use realistic multi-word names, live parsed totals, numbered rows, delete actions, eligibility counts, full purchase terms, and actual product pricing.

journeyTest.evidence: The same roster count and numbered identities persist through input, classic draw, wheel mode, active pool, and the 17-contestant upgrade threshold.

platformTest.evidence: Original-resolution iPhone 17 Pro and iPad Pro 13-inch renders preserve native safe areas, scrolling, toggles, text editing, minimum 46-point custom actions, and tablet-scale content width.

buyerValueTest.evidence: The rendered app now communicates a cohesive live-picking product through branded task surfaces, purposeful status, explicit modes, persistent pool controls, and a purchase sheet that matches the winner experience.

implementationTest.evidence: The visual grammar is implemented as shared SwiftUI tokens, panel modifiers, button tones, selected-mode styling, gradients, border weights, radii, and hard-shadow depth; the simulator build succeeds.

screenFindings.finding: The first phone render established the intended celebration-native hierarchy: black display type, blue title offset, yellow status pills, lavender-to-white panels, ink borders, and distinct primary/destructive actions.
Wheel mode is visibly selected with the warm raised state; the editor, draw setup, wheel surface, and persistent pool controls share one component grammar without obscuring names or delete targets.

The final tablet render uses the full content column effectively, keeps the spin target dominant, preserves scannable active-pool rows, and gives every action a consistent full-width capsule geometry.
The upgrade sheet retains complete pricing, renewal, restore, privacy, and EULA information while adopting the same gradient panel, ink outline, violet depth, and capsule actions as the main app.

repairs: Replaced the flat green page, pale one-pixel cards, translucent modals, and mixed system button tints with a shared celebration-derived token system.
Converted draw mode from a generic segmented control into explicit Quick Pick and Spin Wheel states with warm selection and inked outlines.
Added task-specific readiness and eligibility pills, contestant-entry helper copy, and active-pool totals without adding promotional chrome.
Rejected the first tablet render because shared buttons only wrapped their labels; repaired the button primitive so actions fill their allotted geometry on every form factor.
Added a DEBUG-only wheel fixture guard after the first tablet wheel capture incorrectly advanced into a winner reveal, preserving deterministic visual inspection without changing production behavior.
verdict: PASS — the main NameSnap workflow now matches the winner celebration's color, gradient, outline, radius, and hard-depth philosophy while remaining readable, task-specific, and responsive on iPhone and iPad.
